newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine harvest slows on rain, grain crop seen up.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine harvest slows on rain, grain crop seen up.

text.p: Heavy soil moisture from recent downpours is delaying Ukraine's grain harvest, but the former Soviet republic still expects a good crop, Agriculture Minister Mykhailo Zubets said on Thursday.
"It is a difficulty for us -- moisture is delaying effective harvesting," Zubets, also a deputy prime minister, told a news conference.
"By now we should have gathered one million tonnes of grain but we have only 300,000 tonnes."
But Zubets said Ukraine was delighted with grain yields so far, which he called significantly higher than last year's level although he did not specify sizes.
Ukraine, its harvest begun, has forecast 1997 net grain output of 35 million tonnes against last year's drought-damaged 25.4 million tonnes.
Previous forecasts put exports from this year's crop at six million tonnes compared to three million tonnes last year. Russia is a big buyer of Ukrainian material.

Zubets said Ukraine planned to increase the area sown to winter wheat later this year as part of an overall plan to bring the country once known as the breadbasket of the Soviet Union back to 50-million-tonne harvests.
The Agriculture Ministry has forecast winter wheat output at 20 million tonnes this year, after 13.4 million tonnes in 1996.
"We should be able to increase grain exports to 15 million tonnes per year," Zubets said, referring to plans to boost output in the future.
He said Ukraine would also concentrate on planting more sunflowerseeds to capitalise on world demand.
Ukraine has forecast a 1997 sunflowerseed harvest of three million tonnes against 2.3 million tonnes last year.
"These two (winter wheat and sunflowers) will form the basis for reforms in the agro-industrial sector," Zubets said.
